title: Making illustrated CCTV testable: Dead Circuit 2.1’s lamp and torch signals
author: RobeertIV
selftext:
Dead Circuit 2.1 is an AI-assisted Unity surveillance mystery built around illustrated CCTV scenes. Codex contributed code, campaign writing and interface work; Higgsfield generated the illustration plates; audio is original deterministic synthesis. No AI content is generated while playing. The design problem is making a camera image useful as evidence when its underlying scene is an illustration.



The field-test interaction gives the player an explicit request, a visible response where appropriate, and a retained written observation. A worker can be asked for two torch flashes; another test requests a lamp signal. These effects are rendered by the game around the plate. Reduced motion keeps written observations and static result markers available, and players can compare the captured frames manually. The scenes do not contain fully animated character performances.



That also shaped the trailer checks. It uses native 2.1 captures, and the encoded torch sequence was compared with source-image pixels at both pulse windows and the dark interval between them. Editorial crops and magnified details help show the actual test. Route movement is labelled as a schematic control-room overlay. The aim is to give the viewer enough context to distinguish the image, the requested action and the returned observation.



For this kind of low-motion evidence interface, what would you want recorded alongside a response to make your next decision: a request identifier, more explicit timing, or a different comparison view? This is a commercial project: Windows, US$1.99 or more, with the production disclosure and gameplay trailer on the page: [https://robeertiv.itch.io/dead-circuit-the-seventh-name](https://robeertiv.itch.io/dead-circuit-the-seventh-name)
